milestones.title: Native parity infrastructure
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Same-source runtime and diagnostic oracles; compiler/SDK fingerprinting; bounded fresh-process repetitions and process-tree cleanup; exact shard/repetition/digest receipts; negative controls; durable source-bound gate receipts.

requirements.notes: Exact and partial-order same-source fixtures, digest stability, assertion negatives, and a deliberate mismatch exercise the runtime oracle.
The real compiler typechecks diagnostic fixtures under the pinned strict-concurrency flags and verifies line-specific fragments.
Each interpreted repetition runs in a distinct process with a hard deadline, identity-safe TERM/KILL escalation, and descendant cleanup coverage.
The coordinator proves exact disjoint manifest coverage, per-case repetitions, native digests, and strict single-marker receipts.
Pinned or record-only toolchain identity, source start/end fingerprints, stage diagnostics, and durable GREEN/RED receipts are machine checked.

milestones.title: Task-owned evaluator context
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Task-owned evaluator contexts, cancellation isolation, async-initializer ownership, and detached host re-entry have native parity and focused ownership coverage.

requirements.notes: Task-local evaluator ownership, cancellation isolation, detached re-entry, and async initializer interleaving are all covered.

milestones.title: Task runtime
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Task outcomes, cancellation request versus observation, post-completion cancellation, completed-handle session/driver release, waiter and handle lifetimes, detached and top-level policy, priority donation, and task-local inheritance/unwind have native parity and focused ownership proof.

requirements.notes: Typed outcomes, waiter edges, source cancellation, detached tasks, source-handle lifetime, and missing-await diagnostics are covered.
Initial inheritance, priority donation, declaration identity, scoped binding, and unwind are covered.
Late task-handle cancellation updates the orthogonal cancellation state while preserving the immutable successful outcome and terminal state, including after active-registry release.

Release atomically replaces active runtime ownership with a value-only task snapshot. Weak references prove that the record, interpreter runtime/session, and native driver deallocate while repeated completed reads and late cancellation remain valid.

milestones.title: Suspension, clocks, and cancellation handlers
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Runtime-owned task waits, host suspension, cancellable sleep, yield progress, cancellation-handler timing and cleanup, and seeded replayable cancellation-race exploration have native parity and focused runtime coverage.

requirements.notes: Controlled suspension, cancellable sleep, yield progress, handler timing, nesting, and cleanup are covered. The pinned swiftlang executable board additionally preserves the deprecated positional nonthrowing sleep cancellation contract.

The ordinary gate explores 64 deterministic seeds spanning cancel-before/after-complete, four cancel/wake boundaries, handler unregister ordering, and repeated cancellation requests. Every invariant failure reports an exact one-seed replay command; native fixtures independently anchor the terminal, sleep, and handler semantics.

milestones.title: Structured concurrency
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Async-let ownership and lexical cleanup plus nonthrowing and throwing task-group joining, iteration, cancellation, all eight generated `isEmpty`/`isCancelled` state properties, all four `cancelAll()` declarations, all four canonical `addTask(priority:operation:)` declarations for the evidenced nonisolated subset, all four ordinary/throwing group `next()` declarations, both deprecated `spawn()`, both deprecated `async()`, both deprecated conditional `add()` aliases, both deprecated `asyncUnlessCancelled()` aliases, and both deprecated `spawnUnlessCancelled()` aliases, explicit ordinary and throwing `makeAsyncIterator()` capabilities plus all six generated iterator `next`/`cancel` rows with value-semantic terminal state, default plus explicit-MainActor `waitForAll()` behavior, and `ThrowingTaskGroup.nextResult()` result projection with the arbitrary-actor executor gaps recorded, nested Task/async-let/group ownership, child-created unstructured lifetime, task-local and executor inheritance, error projection, draining, bounded stress, replayable cancellation storms, weak lifetime release, and process-isolated RSS/heap plateaus have native parity, focused runtime evidence, or an explicit negative disposition.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: Close the generated task-group API tail by assigning every remaining overload an explicit implementation/verification disposition, cover repeated-wait/new-work behavior, and finish the M7-backed escaped-capability boundary; positive claims require executable evidence and negative/deferred claims require owned gap or deferral evidence.

requirements.notes: Value projection and normal, return, throw, cancellation, and lexical-defer cleanup paths are covered.
Nonthrowing group joining, result consumption, cancellation state, late children, and defer composition are covered.
Throwing next/wait/iteration behavior, body failure, cancellation projection, drain behavior, and cleanup are covered.

Nested groups, async lets, task-local snapshotting, group-child-created unstructured lifetime, and MainActor/cooperative executor selection across Task-to-async-let-to-group composition have native parity plus focused ownership and cleanup proof.

The generated active-interface inventory now retains every task-group overload plus the nested ordinary/throwing Iterator next/cancel surface, including async, throws/rethrows, isolation, function-type isolation, Sendable, actor, modifier, and default-value metadata; active-SDK staleness and synthetic edge cases are tested. Same-source parity covers isEmpty/isCancelled and cancelAll on all four group kinds, the supported nonisolated subset of all four canonical addTask(priority:operation:) rows, deprecated spawn and async alias pairs, deprecated async add, asyncUnlessCancelled, and throwing spawnUnlessCancelled aliases with pre-cancel true/value/error and post-cancel false/empty behavior, explicit ordinary/throwing makeAsyncIterator creation, the shared exactly-once stream, terminal state after nil/error/cancel, value-semantic iterator copies, cancellation, default next, and explicit-MainActor next, all four group next declarations including protocol-witness selection of both disfavored ABI overloads, default and explicit-MainActor nonthrowing/throwing waitForAll behavior, and ThrowingTaskGroup.nextResult empty/success/failure/cancellation result projection with single consumption. Pinned unchanged swiftlang inputs independently prove MainActor-isolated group use, pending next suspension and drain, recovery after a throwing next, ordinary/throwing groups drained through the interpreter's direct async-iteration path, deprecated spawn iteration, the ordinary async alias state transition, addTaskUnlessCancelled rejection after owner cancellation, and ordinary spawnUnlessCancelled before/after cancelAll contrasted with unconditional spawn. Arbitrary actor executors remain outside the current runtime model. Add repeated waits/new work and a runtime or diagnostic disposition for every remaining mechanically exposed overload.

The unchanged pinned swiftlang fixture proves native inout TaskGroup capture diagnostics through the production preflight engine, while runtime lifetime checks remain covered separately. Synthetic callable, property, and nominal type contracts now fail closed; close the requirement when target-aware real-project manifests carry the same boundary.

A native-anchored bounded fanout/depth tree and 16 repeated interpreter sessions cover structured completion and empty task/group/scope/scheduler registries. Weak references prove release of the complete task/group/scope/context/driver graph and its interpreter/runtime owner. A 64-seed replayable cancellation board varies fanout, before-add versus after-start cancellation, and duplicate requests while proving complete draining. A process-isolated 896-session probe executes 41,216 structured nodes while sampling RSS, physical footprint, and live heap across twelve measured batches; three focused runs plateaued at zero median RSS/footprint drift and 448 bytes of heap drift. A synthetic linear-retention negative control proves the plateau analyzer fails closed.

milestones.title: Actor support and executor architecture
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Logical cooperative-default and MainActor executor identity, source hops, caller restoration, and detached-task lane identity are covered.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: Next major cycle: add actor identity/storage, serial executor queues, isolated hops, reentrancy/resume ownership, isolated parameters, arbitrary global actors, and stress; physical workers remain M9.

requirements.notes: Logical cooperative-default and MainActor hops are covered without claiming physical worker execution.
First cycle slice: valid actor declarations must not execute with class-like semantics; reject unsupported actor execution until actor-owned identity/storage and executor dispatch are installed.
Add actor IDs, actor-owned storage, serial mailbox/executor queues, lifetime cleanup, and isolated entry hops.
Add suspension-safe actor reentrancy/resume ownership, isolated parameters, arbitrary global actors, and replayable mailbox stress.

milestones.title: Async sequences and continuations
milestones.ledgerEvidence: No protocol-level AsyncSequence or continuation runtime is claimed; task-group-specific iteration remains M4 evidence only.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: Requires M5 actor/executor resume ownership, then protocol iteration, streams, continuations, cancellation, and cleanup coverage.

requirements.notes: Group-specific iteration is M4 evidence and does not count as protocol-level AsyncSequence or continuation support.

milestones.title: Compiler-backed concurrency checking
milestones.ledgerEvidence: The production interpreter now has explicit required and diagnostics-only compiler preflight, a bounded source/toolchain/SDK/target/gateway cache, registry-bound compiled host modules with separately fingerprinted compiler modes, a generated SDK re-export surface, multi-file project checking, pinned TaskGroup, Sendable, effectful-property, and imported-type-isolation diagnostics, generated active-SDK top-level/Task/task-group plus nested group-iterator declaration metadata, typed synthetic top-level and receiver-qualified callable/property declarations, fail-closed synthetic nominal struct/class/enum declarations that preserve enclosing attributes, and authored implementation/verification dispositions for all 32 Task instance/static rows plus forty-one task-group and iterator state, cancellation, wait, nextResult, spawn, async, add, canonical addTask, asyncUnlessCancelled, spawnUnlessCancelled, makeAsyncIterator, next, and cancel rows.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: Review the remaining 83 generated top-level and task-group overload rows and add target-aware build manifests before M5 or M8 closure.

requirements.notes: The parity harness retains the actor-isolation oracle, and the same production compiler engine used by Interpreter validates unchanged SHA-pinned swiftlang TaskGroup capture and imported MainActor-type diagnostics. The generated nominal type reproduces the imported-type diagnostic, and required mode rejects before interpreter state or task creation.

Active-SDK top-level function, Task static/instance, task-group, and nested ordinary/throwing group-iterator declaration slices are generated with an explicit incomplete-scope denominator and stale checks. Production preflight composes registry-bound host modules, SDK re-exports, multi-file projects, typed synthetic top-level functions, receiver-qualified callables/properties, and empty non-generic nominal struct/class/enum declarations before interpreter mutation. Exact member effects and enclosing attributes are retained from SwiftSyntax. Legal typed HostProperty async reads enter a task-bound host suspension and cover instance/static, nested, optional, success, and caught-error paths; synchronous entry fails closed. Nominal members are emitted inside their type bodies so type isolation is inherited and class designated initializers remain legal; conflicting, non-public, actor, protocol, generic, inherited, and non-empty nominal contracts fail closed. SHA-pinned swiftlang modules prove cross-module MainActor behavior for functions, static properties, imported types, positional nonthrowing sleep cancellation, ordinary TaskGroup.isEmpty/cancelAll/async, ThrowingTaskGroup.nextResult recovery, ordinary/throwing group iteration plus deprecated spawn iteration, addTaskUnlessCancelled rejection after owner cancellation, and ordinary spawnUnlessCancelled before/after cancelAll. All 32 active-SDK Task instance/static rows and forty-one task-group plus iterator state, cancellation, wait, nextResult, spawn, async, add, canonical addTask, asyncUnlessCancelled, spawnUnlessCancelled, makeAsyncIterator, next, and cancel rows now have explicit native-parity or negative dispositions; the remaining 83 generated rows and target-aware project build manifests remain open.
